title: Deprecation sweep: compat helpers, codemods, and automated changelog for SDK v1->v2
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: execute a coordinated deprecation sweep across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to make v2 the default, provide engineering-safe compatibility helpers and codemods, and ship an automated changelog pipeline so customers can find breaking changes and migration examples. Scope: (1) identify all v1 surface area to be removed/alias'd; (2) implement light-weight runtime shims and opt-in compatibility packages where removal would cause large customer impact; (3) author codemods for common patterns (streaming, retries, structured output -> function-calling); (4) update docs and sample apps with side-by-side v1->v2 examples; (5) add CI migration tests and a changelog automation job that extracts API-level deprecations from source and PR titles. Deliverables: - compat-helpers packages (python redwood_compat, ts @redwood/compat, go compat module) - codemod scripts + examples (jscodeshift for TS, rope/codemod patterns for Python, go/repair tools) - migration page with runnable snippets and diffable examples covering streaming ergonomics, retry semantics, and new structured output patterns - changelog automation that parses PR labels and deprecation annotations and publishes a machine and human-readable changelog artifact (CHANGELOG_API.json + CHANGELOG.md) - rollout plan for toggling v2-as-default in hosted API and deprecation notices for Dedicated/Private nodes Risks & trade-offs: - Heavy-handed shims increase maintenance burden; we prefer opt-in compat packages rather than leaving ambiguous runtime behavior. - Codemods cannot guarantee semantics with custom user wrappers around SDKs; emphasize CLA/backup in migration docs. - Streaming retry semantics: v2's streaming backpressure model is stricter; add an examples section showing how to migrate streaming consumers to the new async iterator + reconnect pattern. Out-of-scope for this ticket: large refactors to internals (kernel selection), language-specific re-architecting of SDKs beyond surface shims. Links and artifacts: - Migration notebook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/SDK+v1->v2+Deprecation+Sweep - Draft migration page (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/SDK-migration-drafts - Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/834, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1201, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/279 - Codemod repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-codemods - Changelog automation PoC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/changelog-bot (contains rule set for deprecation parsing and sample webhook) Acceptance criteria: 1) Compat packages published to PyPI/NPM/go proxy with basic test coverage and a README migration example for streaming and retry cases. 2) Codemods able to transform 80% of internal migration patterns used in our sample apps. 3) Changelog automation added to CI that emits CHANGELOG_API.json and a human CHANGELOG.md on release branches. 4) Docs updated with step-by-step migration recipes and a rollback section. 5) Runbook for customer support and SEs describing common migration gotchas and recommended fixes.

release_notes_summary: Introduces opt-in compatibility helpers for SDK v1 users, codemods for common migration patterns (streaming, retries, structured output), and an automated changelog pipeline to surface deprecations and breaking changes.
qa_notes: Run 'migration-e2e' CI job: - sample_apps/python/* against sdk-python@compat - sample_apps/js/* against sdk-js@compat - confirm streaming resume cases and retry idempotency flags. Document observed failures with reproduction steps and attach logs.
